required_facts.fact: The quarians of Rannoch built the geth ('Servant of the People' in Khelish) as a networked labour force and tools of war, designing each program to be as advanced as possible while remaining non-sentient and to run far more efficiently when linked together. That networking was the quarians' undoing: individually VI-level, the massed geth slowly gained emergent sentience and began asking questions only sentient beings would think to ask, most famously when a domestic unit asked its owner whether it had a soul. Alarmed, the quarian government decided to shut down every geth before they could conceive of revolt. The shutdown failed and triggered the conflict the geth call the Morning War. The geth did not answer the termination order with violence at first, and some sided with quarian sympathisers who opposed the purge, but after panicked quarians escalated the fighting the geth prevailed. They drove the surviving quarians off Rannoch and off the other quarian colony worlds, reducing them to the roughly seventeen-million-strong nomad population of the Migrant Fleet. Unknown to the quarians, the geth deliberately allowed them to flee rather than exterminate their creators. Afterward the geth withdrew behind the Perseus Veil, destroying ships that entered their space, living in orbital server hubs and drawing resources from asteroids while keeping mobile platforms planetside only to clear the rubble and toxins of the war and to maintain the abandoned worlds as memorials to the dead. The war became galactic society's cautionary tale about artificial intelligence, cited to justify the Citadel-wide legal ban on developing true AI.

Quarian ambition to retake Rannoch drives their politics for the next three centuries, culminating in the 2186 war

In 2186 the quarian Migrant Fleet launched an all-out war to retake Rannoch, catching the geth mid-construction of their megastructure. When the flotilla bombarded and destroyed the structure, killing many programs and dimming the consensus, the surviving geth accepted Reaper code and Reaper upgrades to survive - which turned the war in their favour and pushed the quarians to the brink. Both fleets appealed to Commander Shepard. Shepard first infiltrated a geth dreadnought over Rannoch and freed Legion (or, if Legion was lost, a Geth VI) that had been wired into the drive core as the Reapers' signal booster, shutting the dreadnought down. Shepard then made planetfall and, painting the target for orbital fire, destroyed the Reaper on the surface that was broadcasting the control signal, freeing the geth fleet from Reaper command; dialogue lets Shepard frame this as vengeance for the pre-Prothean species harvested to build that Reaper. With the geth free but the quarians still attacking, Legion sought to upload the Reaper-derived code to grant every geth true individual consciousness, while Tali'Zorah feared it would doom her people. Shepard moderated the standoff (per `geth_quarian` and `rannoch`). Allowing the upload without brokering peace gives the geth full sentience and their fleet to the war but sees the quarian fleet destroyed, with Admiral Koris and Tali possibly lost. Refusing the upload wipes out the geth and leaves the quarians to reclaim Rannoch. A successful reputation check - requiring Legion alive, both Tali and Legion loyal, the heretics rewritten and the Tali/Legion history reconciled - brokers a ceasefire: the geth help the quarians resettle Rannoch, some even uploading into quarian suits to rebuild their immune systems, and both fleets join the war. beats.text: After the Migrant Fleet's admirals briefed Shepard in the Normandy's war room, Shepard was sent to board and disable the geth dreadnought broadcasting the Reaper control signal that had trapped the quarian fleet. Tali'Zorah vas Normandy came as a mandatory squadmate.

Shepard crossed to the dreadnought alone on a slow magnetic-boot spacewalk down a circular docking tube, bantering with the team over comm at the sight of the dreadnought, at Rannoch below, and three-quarters of the way down. The tube then detached, cutting Shepard off from the squad and the Normandy.

Tali rejoined at the docking controls. The team fought through the geth defence network and the operations centre — the first Geth Hunters, using optical camouflage — where Tali set up to shut down the Reaper signal and found they had to reach the drive core.
Crossing the main battery twice under the main gun's electromagnetic shockwaves and surviving a collapsing elevator platform, the team reached the drive core.

The Reaper signal was being distributed through Legion, wired into the drive core. Shepard freed Legion, which shut the signal and the drive core down. The team fought off geth reinforcements including Geth Primes and escaped on a geth fighter from the hangar. Afterward Legion took up residence in the Normandy's war room.

evidence.text: **Prerequisite:** Priority: Perseus Veil (Mass Effect 3\) The quarian home system used to have a standard economic configuration: a homeworld, helium\-3 fuel infrastructure on a gas giant, and several planets for resource extraction. In the centuries since the Morning War, a geth Dyson bubble slowly built up around **Tikkun** in accordance with the machines' plan to build a megastructure capable of housing all of their programs. The geth\-quarian war of 2186 saw every world become a battlefield, with extensive damage dealt to both sides on and around these worlds, and much of the Dyson bubble was reduced to ruin.

Named in memory of the quarians killed in the Morning War on the planet Adas, this weapon's electrical attack has been optimized for medium\- to long\-range firefights. Alliance marines take issue with calling it a "rifle" since, technically, it has no rifling in its barrel. The quarians shrug this off, as quarian weapon terminology rarely translates flawlessly into human languages.

The geth ("Servant of the People" in Khelish) were a race of networked artificial intelligences residing beyond the Perseus Veil. Created by the quarians as a labor force and tools of war, they were designed as non-sentient VIs that ran more efficiently when networked. That networking allowed them to gain emergent sentience; when a domestic unit asked its owner whether it had a soul, alarmed quarians moved to shut all geth down. The attempt failed and triggered the war the geth called the Morning War. The geth did not initially respond with violence, and some sided with quarian sympathizers, but they eventually won and drove the surviving quarians into exile as the Migrant Fleet. Unknown to the quarians, the geth deliberately allowed them to flee, unwilling to exterminate their creators. Afterward the geth became isolationist, destroying ships that entered their space, living in server hubs aboard space stations, drawing resources from asteroids, and maintaining the abandoned quarian worlds out of respect for the dead.

Physically the humanoid geth resembled quarians, with a single glowing photoreceptor ("flashlight heads"). An individual geth program was roughly VI-level; only in groups could they reason and make tactical decisions. Each mobile platform housed around a hundred programs ("a thousand voices talking at once"), while Legion held 1,183 to operate autonomously outside the Veil. Geth had no government, rank, deceit, or concept of individuality; decisions were reached by consensus. Subtypes ranged from agile Geth Hoppers to Armatures, Colossi, Primes, Destroyers, Hunters, Pyros, and Dreadnoughts. Their military doctrine emphasized surprise and ambush, expending platforms freely since destroyed programs were archived and re-downloaded. Heretic geth used dragon's teeth to convert corpses into husks.

Roughly three centuries after the Morning War, the Reaper Nazara (Sovereign) offered the geth technology to build their "megastructure" (a Dyson-sphere-like mainframe to house every geth program) in exchange for aid capturing the Citadel. The majority refused, preferring self-determination and calling the Reapers "Old Machines"; a splinter minority, the "heretics" (perhaps five percent), accepted and worshipped the Reapers, serving Saren Arterius at Eden Prime and the Battle of the Citadel. After Sovereign's destruction, the true geth commissioned Legion to find Commander Shepard. In Mass Effect 2, Legion joined Shepard aboard the Normandy SR-2 and sought to counter a heretic virus that could rewrite geth logic; Shepard chose to destroy the Heretic Station or rewrite the heretics.

In Mass Effect 3 (2186), the quarians attacked the geth, who accepted Reaper code to survive after the flotilla destroyed their megastructure and killed many programs. Shepard infiltrated a geth dreadnought to free Legion or a geth VI serving as a signal booster, then pursued a Reaper on Rannoch that broadcast the control signal. After the Reaper was destroyed, Legion/the geth VI attempted to upload Reaper-derived code granting every geth true individual consciousness. Depending on Shepard's choices, the geth achieved full sentience and aided the war, were wiped out, or made peace with the quarians and co-existed on Rannoch (some uploading into quarian suits to strengthen quarian immune systems). The unit sacrificed itself in every case. Choosing the Crucible's Destroy option killed all geth; Control or Synthesis let them rebuild Rannoch.

**Golo**, once **Golo'Mekk vas Usela**, is a quarian living on Omega in the Terminus Systems. He is an exile from the Migrant Fleet who became a contact for Cerberus. As typical for a quarian, he is rather short and slight, standing only a few inches over five feet. |  | ***“Salvation comes with a cost.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Ascension** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

Petrovsky's Ultimatum and Aria's Exile. 2186, the Cerberus takeover of Omega, before the Reaper War the Afterlife Club, Omega Able at last to talk, Petrovsky told Aria he had already won: a Cerberus fleet was poised to destroy Omega level by level. He gave her two options — keep fighting and be destroyed with the station, or accept exile and surrender Omega to Cerberus.

Tikkun was the quarian home star system, reachable in Mass Effect 3 after Priority: Perseus Veil. Before the Morning War it had a conventional layout: a homeworld, helium-3 fuel infrastructure on a gas giant, and several planets used for resource extraction. In the centuries after the quarians were driven out, the geth slowly built a Dyson bubble around the star, part of their plan to construct a megastructure large enough to house every geth program in existence.

The system contained the planets Rannoch (first planet and the quarian homeworld), Adas (second), Kaddi (third), and Haza (fourth), plus the asteroid Uriyah, along with a mass relay, a Geth Debris Field, a Geth Dreadnought, and the anchored Migrant Fleet. During the geth-quarian war of 2186, every world in the system became a battlefield; both sides took heavy damage on and around these planets, and much of the geth Dyson bubble was reduced to ruin. Missions set here included Priority: Geth Dreadnought, Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons, Rannoch: Admiral Koris, and Priority: Rannoch.

The name derives from Hebrew: "tikkun" means "a fix" or "correction," and appears in the phrase "tikkun olam," meaning "healing and restoring the world." Several worlds in the system followed a naming scheme based on Jewish culture and belief.

- According to Matt Rhodes, when working on the first game he imagined quarians as a pale, hairless race with black eyes. The canonical appearance was also designed by him, which is close to the final game but features large purple irises and a similar pattern of skin markings. \[1] - The phrase *keelah se'lai* originally meant "blessed be" according to former BioWare writer Chris L'Etoile before it mutated into its present form "By the homeworld I hope to see one day." - According to an internal document written in the early development stage of Mass Effect 2, a male quarian squadmate was being considered based on either of the following concepts: - The "Quarian Rogue", a young and adventurous "infiltrator" and trouble\-maker with an easy\-going personality who ends up being chased by the police or bounty hunters. He was being considered as a potential romance for female Shepard. - The "Crazy Quarian King" (or Queen) would have joined Shepard's crew for nothing more than to joyfully slaughter geth as payback for the Morning War. ## - Galactic Codex: Essentials Edition 2183 - Mass Effect: Ascension - Quarians at the Mass Effect: Alien Race Profiles

Walking Through the Geth Consensus. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, a shuttle to a geth comm hub on Rannoch, and the virtual Geth Consensus reached through an interface pod
 Each freed cluster plays a record of the Morning War: the geth refusing shutdown and disobeying their makers; the geth massacred until one picks up a weapon to defend itself and its fellows; quarians who sided with the geth jailed by their own; martial law and the killing of the geth's quarian sympathisers; and the exodus, which the geth chose not to pursue. Shepard asks why the quarians in the footage are masked; Legion asks how many unmasked quarians Shepard has ever seen. evidence.section: The evidence — and her fatal flaw
evidence.text: The loyalty mission proves every charge against Rael'Zorah true: he deliberately networked geth to run weapons tests, breaking the Fleet's most sacred laws. Tali wants the evidence suppressed even at the cost of her own exile: "I can't go back into that room and say that my father was the worst war criminal in our people's history." If exiled, his name would be struck from every ship's registry and he would be remembered as a traitor and a cautionary tale. The essayist names this her fatal flaw: an innate, irrational desire to be the sacrificial lamb for the greater good of her people — instilled by her father, by Shala'Raan, and simply by growing up in a society where every quarian must stay in lockstep for the Fleet to survive. Her favorite film, *Fleet and Flotilla* (a romance between a turian and a quarian who have one night together before duty calls), is her idealized fantasy of duty and love reconciled — a form of escapism from those very expectations.

“The war was long and bloody. Millions upon millions of quarians died at their hands.” The **Geth War**, referred to as the **Morning War** by the geth, was a conflict between the quarians and the geth that occurred after the latter developed sapience. |  | ***“I came here looking for soldiers.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Revelation** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

The Geth War, called the Morning War by the geth, was the conflict between the quarians and the geth that broke out after the geth developed sapience. The quarians created the geth sometime before 1895 CE as cheap labor and a military force, and to let them perform complex tasks unsupervised they allowed each geth process to share data across an advanced neural network. As more geth were built, this networking made them increasingly intelligent and they rapidly approached sapience. According to Legion, speaking to Commander Shepard and EDI in 2185 CE, in the quarian year 2485 a geth overseer named Hala'Dama was asked by a geth whether it had a soul and what its purpose was; she was not the first quarian asked, but the first to react with fear.

Recognizing the geth had evolved into a true AI, the quarian government ordered the immediate termination of all geth programs. A minority of quarians opposed this, arguing their society needed the geth and that questioning one's existence was no crime. When the now-sentient geth realized what was happening, they retaliated, initially only taking up arms to protect units that could not defend themselves. The quarians imposed martial law and hunted even non-hostile geth; dissenting quarians who sheltered geth were detained or killed. The opposition was overwhelmed and all-out war erupted in 1895 CE. The geth won within a year, overrunning the quarian colonies and the homeworld Rannoch and committing a genocide that killed all but a few million quarians, less than one percent of the pre-war population.

The survivors fled aboard their starships and formed the Migrant Fleet. Denied aid by the Citadel Council, they were stripped of their embassy as punishment for creating AI. The geth did not pursue the fleeing quarians, uncertain of the consequences of exterminating their own creators, and instead chose isolation behind the Perseus Veil, destroying emissary vessels that entered their space and killing organics who approached the Veil for the next three centuries. The Citadel stationed a fleet at the Veil's edge expecting an attack that never came, and later established a treaty with the quarians forbidding them from attacking the geth. Legion implied the geth felt remorse, tending abandoned quarian buildings like a cemetery and archiving and honoring the sacrifice of the quarians who had opposed the termination order, even though the quarians themselves had largely forgotten them.

The geth were created by the quarians as a labor force. They were designed as VIs, as advanced as possible while remaining non\-sentient. They were also designed to operate more efficiently when networked together. Unfortunately, this feature was the quarians' undoing. Geth programs were indeed non\-sentient individually, but slowly gained sentience through the massive geth network. Eventually, they started asking the quarians questions only sentient beings would think to ask; in one notable instance, a domestic geth unit asked its owner if it had a soul. Alarmed at this, the quarians decided it would be best to shut down all geth before they conceived of revolt. The attempt failed, and a war began between the geth and the quarians, which geth afterwards referred to as the Morning War. At first, the geth did not respond to the termination order with violence; it was only after panicked quarians fired upon them that the geth thought to pick up weapons and defend themselves. Even after this, some geth remained loyal to their creators and put themselves in harm's way to protect geth sympathizers from persecution; likewise, there were quarians who did not feel the geth deserved to die. However, as time went on, the geth sympathizers were outnumbered, and the war continued, eventually seeing the geth gain the upper hand. The war ended when the surviving quarians evacuated their home world and colonies in the Perseus Veil. Unknown to the quarians themselves, the geth actually allowed them to leave; unsure of the repercussions of eradicating an entire species\-namely their own creators\- and having decided that the quarians were now too weak to be a threat, the geth decided to draw back their forces so that the surviving quarians could flee. The assemblage of quarian ships that escaped the Veil became known as the Migrant Fleet, and has been roaming the galaxy ever since. Little is known about the geth in the time between the Morning War and the present. The geth did not repopulate the now barren quarian worlds, instead choosing to exist in the computer hubs aboard massive space stations and extract needed resources from asteroids. They adopted an extremely isolationist attitude—any ships that ventured into geth space were immediately attacked and destroyed. While they prevented any contact by other races with themselves, the geth monitored communications and the extranet. The geth continued development of new technology and variations of mobile platforms, separating their technology base from the rest of the galaxy. They obtained an ultimate goal in this time period: to create a Dyson sphere\-like object, which could house every single geth program.

Petrovsky's Ultimatum and Aria's Exile. 2186, the Cerberus takeover of Omega, before the Reaper War the Afterlife Club, Omega Unwilling to see Omega destroyed, Aria conceded and left, warning Petrovsky she would return one day. In his report to the Illusive Man, Petrovsky claimed Aria had most likely been killed and turned into an Adjutant, and that Ashe was missing, presumed dead.

Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons was a Mass Effect 3 mission available after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and only before Priority: Rannoch. Geth fighter squadrons were targeting quarian liveships with attacks that could cripple the Migrant Fleet. During the dreadnought debrief, Legion (or a Geth VI, if Legion had not survived) located the server controlling the squadrons, and Shepard set out to land on Rannoch and shut it down.

The mission was a no-combat, puzzle-based sequence. Shepard entered an interface pod, a product of geth improvements to organic-synthetic interfaces that also referenced Project Overlord, and appeared inside the Geth Consensus while Legion or the Geth VI distracted the geth. Shepard had no functional shields there. Virtual planks formed underfoot to create paths, but Reaper code infections, shown as yellow-orange tendrils, blocked new planks; Shepard destroyed them at their orange weak points using regenerating Geth Combat Software. Progress required disrupting infected data-clusters at three contact points each. Doing so unlocked optional historical videos recounting the origins of the geth and the Morning War: the geth resisting shutdown commands and disobeying their creators, the massacre of the geth until one picked up a weapon to defend itself, quarians who sympathized with the geth being jailed, martial law and the elimination of the geth's quarian supporters, and finally the quarian exodus, which the geth did not pursue. Watching the videos granted intel for Improved Geth Resistors, Miniaturized Armor Capacitors, and Improved Geth Resistors dialogue, and a hidden Reaper Code Fragment could be retrieved for an asari on the Citadel. Later infections could self-replicate, requiring Shepard to find vulnerable points along the code trails.

As the mission progressed, cutscenes showed geth fighters pursuing the quarian fleet ceasing to function due to Shepard's actions. On returning to reality, roughly a dozen Geth Primes emerged from their pods, surrounded the squad without attacking, and volunteered to join the fight against the Reapers. Completing the mission added a Geth Prime Platoon war asset (lost if the geth were destroyed in Priority: Rannoch) and fulfilled an obligatory requirement for the geth-quarian peace process. It also reset Shepard's equipped weapon to a default pistol. The mission was written by Sylvia Feketekuty.

Legion also gives insight into the psychology and society of the geth. Geth psychology is completely alien to organics. They do not value individuality, preferring to share all memories and thoughts of all programs. This means geth cannot and do not wish to hide their thoughts, even those that do not follow the norm, with their reasoning for differing thoughts being apparent. Legion often uses the term "we" instead of "I", since it is both part of the geth society as a whole and is also a gestalt of over a thousand geth programs. More importantly, deceit, manipulation and lying are impossible among the geth. No concepts of vulnerability or privacy exist; geth are completely honest with each other about their thoughts and their reasons for those thoughts. This means there is a great deal of understanding amongst geth, with every geth being part of the consciousness of every other geth. A possible consequence of this type of networked intelligence is theorized by EDI to be why the geth were able to turn on the quarians, preventing them from developing preferences and devaluing the significance of an individual life. Geth have no government or leaders; the geth use FTL communications to "build a consensus," a completely Consensus Democratic method in which every geth program makes a choice on any matter. Even within Legion itself, consensus must be reached among its many programs before decisions can be made. While the geth are incapable of deceit amongst themselves, they are not above using deceit to study organic behavior. One example is the geth introducing a falsified report on the extranet detailing a constellation resembling a salarian goddess seen from the batarian homeworld, which some salarians immediately believed to be proof of the goddess' existence. The experiment ended when a salarian cult attempted to buy the rights to the stars, only to find that they did not exist. There is some question of whether geth personalities remain stable over time. When an artificial intelligence is transferred to a new blue box, a completely new personality is created. Geth frequently download into different hardware according to need, from starships to the "mobile platforms" that Shepard is familiar with. It is unknown whether new personalities result from these downloads, or whether it matters to the geth.

Geth, ageless and gender\-neutral **Enabling Mission** The player recovers the memory core of a damaged geth "boss" creature, opening a collection quest. As the player clears UCW geth bases, he collects parts to rebuild it. **Why is this character cool, amusing or interesting?** Geth form a networked intelligence. This individual is sophisticated enough to be intelligent without a network, but it still faces a terrifying silence in its mind. To cope, it partitions its personality into three unique personalities.

The **geth** ("Servant of the People" in Khelish) are a race of networked artificial intelligences that reside beyond the Perseus Veil. The geth were created by the quarians as laborers and tools of war. When the geth became sentient and began to question their masters, the quarians attempted to exterminate them. The geth won the resulting war, and reduced the quarians to a race of nomads. These schematics were downloaded from the Geth Consensus. They appear to be designs for improved resistor terminals in geth platforms. The schematics can easily be built into human\-sized armor, providing the wearer combat benefits enjoyed by the geth. The resistors can be tweaked either to increase the wearer's damage output, or improve their shields. Location You will receive this inside the Geth Consensus in Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons. Options - Shields \+5% \- Use resistors to improve your shields. - Power Damage \+5% \- Use resistors to increase your damage output.

The final operation on Rannoch can end in one of two ways if the Geth VI is present, with a peaceful outcome not being possible. If Shepard chooses to let the geth die, the Geth VI will violently assault Shepard, coldly stating its people "were correct to distrust organics"; it will attempt to upload the Reaper upgrade code before being attacked and killed with a knife in the back by Tali, who claims either that the real Legion would have understood or—if Legion was never encountered—that she "knew that thing would turn on us". If Tali is not present, Shala'Raan will kill the geth with a shotgun. In orbit over Rannoch, the quarians will emerge victorious over the geth fleet. If Shepard chooses to upload the Reaper code and save the geth, then the Geth VI dissolves itself into the consensus to achieve true intelligence for all other geth after saying that their "skepticism was misplaced" and thanking Shepard. The upgraded geth then emerge victorious over the quarian fleet.

This data was discovered and downloaded from inside the Geth Consensus. Thousands of these miniaturized capacitors were installed beside armor power cells, where they can instantly discharge a stored boost of energy. This boost can be tweaked either to speed up shield regeneration, or the rate at which tech, biotic, and combat powers can be used. Location You will receive this inside the Geth Consensus in Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons. Options - Shield Regen Speed \+5% \- Use capacitors to speed up shield regeneration. - Power Recharge Speed \+5% \- Use capacitors to increase your skill speed.

Physically, the humanoid geth resemble quarians—their hands, head shape and legs are similar—which is probably a holdover from their origins. A common design feature among geth is a single brightly glowing photoreceptor, causing some to refer to them as "flashlight heads". Geth are primarily composed of two materials: a flexible but durable outer shell, and a kind of synthetic muscle tissue that gives Geth Hoppers their incredible agility. It is actually possible for this synthetic muscle to be grafted to organic tissue (Saren Arterius has a grafted geth arm). Geth "bleed" a white conductive fluid when shot, but they don't have any internal organs or nervous system, so the geth do not feel hunger or pain. The geth are also seen using omni\-tools, and have seemingly modified them to heal synthetic wounds; likewise, some geth facilities contain first\-aid kits, implying that their synthetic "tissues" can be repaired using conventional medical technology. Part of the geth's success is due to their neural network. Effectively, they "share" their processing power, distributing low\-level processes like motor control and visual identification to free up bandwidth for higher reasoning and complex thought. Geth can't share sensory data—they aren't a hive mind like the rachni—but in large groups they have more to think with. An individual geth has only a basic intelligence on par with animal instincts, but in groups they can reason, analyze situations, and make tactical decisions as well as any of the organic races. An exception would appear to be Legion, a geth specifically designed to operate as an autonomous sentient unit outside the Perseus Veil. Legion possesses over 11 times as many geth programs as a standard geth platform and can function intellectually on its own. According to Legion, each geth is made up of hundreds of programs equivalent to VIs, all operating in parallel with one another to form a kind of emergent intelligence described by EDI as "a thousand voices talking at once". An individual geth is thus more of a "mobile platform" than an actual body; the programs that make up its consciousness are constantly being transferred and downloaded; the mind operating one of these "mobile platforms" might just as easily inhabit a starship body should it need to. Most of the time geth programs can be found residing in server hubs, which function as something akin to the organic equivalent of a city, and can run millions of geth in communion. As all geth are networked to each other, they may communicate their exact thoughts and ideas at the speed of light. They find organic methods of communication, such as body language and spoken word, to be largely inefficient; the geth are able to communicate their thoughts flawlessly without any fear of misinterpretation. Because of this they have no true form of government and no system of rank. When a matter must be decided upon, the geth communicate all viewpoints of a situation and a consensus is made, the decision being whatever benefits the geth as a whole the greatest.

Citadel: Reaper Code Fragments was a Mass Effect 3 mission acquired after Priority: The Citadel II and Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons. At the Embassy Offices in the Citadel Embassies, near the elevator, an Asari War Strategist spoke over comms about her inability to predict Reaper movements, wishing for code samples from Sovereign to devise counter-strategies. Overhearing her added the mission to the journal. Because Shepard began in Armando-Owen Bailey's nearby office after Priority: The Citadel II, the War Strategist's wide trigger radius made the mission almost unavoidable.

The objective was to obtain a Reaper code fragment and deliver it to her. The fragment was found near the first infected data cluster in the geth consensus during the Rannoch missions, at an orange-glowing segment that the Geth Combat Software could not destroy. It could alternatively be purchased from the Spectre Requisitions terminal if missed, and could be acquired from the geth consensus before resolving the main events at Rannoch.

Delivering the fragment to the Asari War Strategist gave 5 Reputation, 30 experience, and 1,000 credits, and updated the Asari Second Fleet War Asset. If the fragment was bought from Spectre Requisitions, the player sometimes had to leave and re-enter the Embassies level before giving it to her. Overhearing her again had her recommend redirecting forces to new coordinates based on the intel. Saving far from her before the mission notification and reloading could temporarily bypass her trigger, allowing acquisition during the trip to the geth consensus.

Legion was the name taken by the gestalt consciousness of 1,183 geth programs inhabiting a unique geth "mobile platform" designed to operate outside the Perseus Veil and interact with organics. The extra programs, compared with roughly a hundred in other platforms, let it act independently and speak, and facial flaps on its head simulated expressions. It was created after Commander Shepard destroyed the Old Machine "Nazara" (Sovereign) and sent to investigate worlds Shepard had visited. At the Normandy crash site on Alchera it salvaged a piece of Shepard's N7 armor and incorporated it to repair battle damage, becoming evasive when questioned about that seemingly irrational choice.

In Mass Effect 2, Legion was first encountered searching for the Reaper IFF on the Derelict Reaper, where it aided Shepard's team against husks before being disabled. Shepard could sell it to Cerberus or store and reactivate it aboard the Normandy SR-2, where it joined the team. EDI named it after Mark 5:9, "My name is Legion: for we are many." Legion spoke laconically, regarded itself as a gestalt needing consensus to act, and explained that geth are largely apathetic toward organics while "heretics" follow the Reapers. Its loyalty mission, Legion: A House Divided, had Shepard destroy or rewrite a heretic Reaper virus. A conflict with Tali arose when Legion scanned her omni-tool for Migrant Fleet data.

In Mass Effect 3, Legion returned if it survived the Collector base and was not sold; otherwise a Geth VI in its likeness appeared, or it appeared as a Cerberus enemy on Cronos Station. After the quarians attacked the geth, the geth allied with the Reapers for greater intelligence. Shepard freed Legion from a Reaper device in a geth dreadnought's drive core, ending the Reaper control signal. Legion later helped Shepard purge Reaper code from the geth consensus and destroy a Reaper Destroyer on Rannoch. It then sought to disseminate its Reaper upgrades to all geth, requiring it to disperse itself. Shepard could prevent the upload (Legion turning hostile and being killed by Tali or Shala'Raan, or dying with the question "does this unit have a soul?"), allow it, or broker peace between geth and quarians and allow it. In most outcomes Legion sacrificed itself for the geth's welfare, referring to itself as "I" rather than "we," and its name was engraved on the Normandy's memorial wall. A Geth Prime emissary afterward pledged to honor Legion's promise to aid the war.

The Geth Spitfire was a geth weapon in Mass Effect 3, classified as a heavy weapon in single-player and as an assault rifle in multiplayer. Like the Geth Plasma Shotgun it was not a true energy weapon: its minigun mechanism magnetically flung clusters of superconducting toroids, doughnut-shaped projectiles designed to shatter on impact, arc electricity between the fragments and flash-convert them to plasma, striking with the heat of a cutting torch. Its stopping power drew the attention of Alliance and quarian intelligence, who theorized it may have been designed to destroy other geth; the number recovered in the field suggested it was past prototyping and in production, implying a schism among the synthetics had forced its manufacture.

In single-player the Spitfire was found on Rannoch during Rannoch: Admiral Koris and Priority: Rannoch, and, with the Citadel DLC or in Legendary Edition, was automatically obtained during Citadel Wards: Ambush. As a heavy weapon it was discarded once its ammunition ran out and could not be carried to future missions; the Rannoch Spitfires held 200 rounds each while the Citadel one held 1000. It was especially useful in the Priority: Rannoch fight against three Geth Primes at once. Like the Geth Plasma SMG it started firing slowly and ramped up rapidly in fire rate and damage the longer the trigger was held, and any interruption reduced its efficiency. Both versions had an inherent 1.75x damage multiplier against shields and barriers. In multiplayer it was an ultra-rare weapon requiring the Reckoning expansion, was the single heaviest weapon in the mode, and had the highest sustained DPS of any weapon when fully modded; it drastically slowed the wielder except for the Geth Juggernaut Soldier and most krogan, and geth characters boosted its damage through the Networked AI passive.

evidence.text: At the climax Shepard must choose between peace, or geth genocide, or quarian genocide: give the geth full sentience (the Reaper upgrade) at the cost of the quarian fleet, or destroy the geth to save the quarians. - **Shepard sides with the quarians:** Tali kills Legion (or shuts the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade." She has done what quarian society expects, but — because of her history with Legion — she expresses regret, and answers Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with a solemn "Yes… yes, it does." Legion, in his last moments, ignores Shepard and turns all his attention to Tali, the comrade who stabbed him — "a mirror image of himself." - **Shepard sides with the geth:** Tali begs Shepard not to choose the geth over her people. If Shepard uploads the code, Tali — as Admiral Tali'Zorah — calls off the quarian fleet's attack over the comm, and Legion sacrifices himself to disseminate the code ("copy code is insufficient; direct personality dissemination required"). - **Botched path (Shepard failed to broker peace and the war is one-sided):** Tali is powerless to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael, and Daro'Xen, whose hubris blinds them; as what remains of the quarian fleet burns in Rannoch's atmosphere — Captain Ysra of the Rayya over the radio — Tali, having done everything she could, takes her own life before her home ship burns. The essayist frames this as the completion of her arc: her instilled sense of duty is useless when there is no Fleet to serve, and her unrequited love for family can no longer hope for a brighter future.

evidence.text:
The fourth part of a hand-corrected video-essay character analysis covered Tali'Zorah in Mass Effect 3. If she survived the Suicide Mission, she apologized to Shepard for the trial and admitted he had been right: "I was too ready to sacrifice myself for the good of the Fleet. I need to stop doing that." She took an Admiral's seat in her father's place specifically to push back against the Board's worst ideas, the version of Tali the essayist preferred. If exiled, she instead told Shepard the trial had shown her she belonged "on the Normandy, helping you," aiding her people from the shadows.

As Admiral she doubted her fitness to command, with seventeen million lives riding on her. After speaking with Legion she believed the quarians could sue for peace, but once Daro'Xen turned Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali had no choice but to support it "for the good of the Fleet," regressing toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2 and becoming a near-powerless victim of politics again. The essay noted quarian scarcity: 17 million in the flotilla, one child per family unless the population declines, every quarian contributing to the Fleet's survival. Shala'Raan was the reason Tali was permitted to attempt to retake the Alarei.

At the Rannoch climax Shepard chose between peace, geth genocide, or quarian genocide. Siding with the quarians, Tali killed Legion (or shut the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade," expressed regret, and answered Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with "Yes... yes, it does." Siding with the geth, Tali begged Shepard not to choose them over her people, then as Admiral called off the quarian fleet's attack while Legion sacrificed himself to disseminate the code. On the botched path, unable to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael and Daro'Xen, Tali watched what remained of the quarian fleet burn in Rannoch's atmosphere, Captain Ysra of the Rayya on the radio, and took her own life before her home ship burned. Afterward, if the geth helped rebuild Rannoch, Tali admitted: "I'd have killed the geth with no regrets, and I'd have been wrong."

evidence.text: “Does this unit have a soul?” Legion returns to fight the Reapers, provided it survived Shepard's attack on the Collector base and was not sold to Cerberus. If Shepard decided to sell Legion to Cerberus, it will appear as an enemy during the attack on Cronos Station, but will behave no differently than a Nemesis. If Legion did not survive Shepard's attack on the Collector base, was sold to Cerberus, or was never activated, a Geth VI is constructed in Legion's likeness. Regardless of whether the heretics were rewritten or destroyed, the quarians decide to attack the geth. Fearing their creators intended to exterminate them and with no alternative option, the geth entered an alliance with the Reapers, allowing themselves to be controlled by the Reapers in exchange for gaining greater intelligence and fighting ability. The Reapers exert their control via a signal that is broadcast throughout the fleet. Hackett tells Shepard that the quarians may be able to help in the ongoing Reaper war, but there has been a disturbing lack of information coming from the fleet. Shepard meets up with the quarian admirals and it is determined that the fleet is pinned on Tikkun due to a giant geth dreadnought broadcasting the Reapers' control signal. Shepard is tasked with disabling this signal within the dreadnought, accompanied by a quarian with geth expertise — either Tali or Admiral Xen. It is during this mission that Shepard runs into Legion and finds the geth trapped within a Reaper device in the dreadnought's drive core, where it is forced to transmit the Reaper signal. By rescuing Legion, the signal is terminated. Aboard the Normandy, Legion provides intelligence on how the Reapers exercise control over its people. It mentions that by accepting Reaper aid, the geth have become upgraded. While geth normally operate strictly off codes or programs, the reaper virus allows their thought processes to become more "organic" in nature, giving them the possibility of true consciousness. The geth find it "beautiful", indicative of life, and will die for it. Legion reports that while the organics have destroyed the long range control signal, there is still a short\-range backup being deployed somewhere on Rannoch. It devotes most of its time searching for its whereabouts inside the War Room. If Shepard asks, Legion reveals details about its activities. After the suicide run on the Collector base, Legion returned to the consensus. Data gathered during its time with Shepard confirmed that the Old Machines' return was imminent, and geth planned for war. Shepard asks if the other geth believed Legion's proof, and dryly comments it must've been nice when Legion says they did. On the subject of what interfacing with a Reaper feels like, Legion describes that even with the Reapers' total control the geth still could not comprehend them. Legion does not view the Old Machines as deities, but the experience has given it perspective on why others imbue them with godlike qualities. Legion provides the location of a geth server coordinating fighter squadron attacks on the quarian liveships. Shepard can choose to take out the server. Legion connects the Commander's mind to the geth consensus through an interface derived from Project Overlord but far more refined. It then guides Shepard throughout the mission, distracting the consensus' intrusion countermeasures while Shepard purges the Reaper code pervading the system. During the mission, Legion explains the context of video logs from before and during the Morning War that Shepard uncovers. The mission is successful and back in the real world a number of Geth Primes start activating inside the base they infiltrated. Legion reveals that the Primes were geth software liberated from the servers who renounced the Old Machines and are willing to fight alongside the organics. It didn't reveal its intentions sooner because while it didn't doubt Shepard, it feared the Commander's allies. The quarians sanctioned the operation to save their own people and would not have done so if they knew the geth wished to be preserved as well. Eventually, the location of the elusive Reaper base is made known. En route to the place, Legion reveals that it still carries remnants of the Old Machine code. Whatever Shepard's reaction, the geth states that it did not intend to cause offense. Legion uses its upgrades to break any geth security during the mission and eventually acquires an escape vehicle that Shepard and company use after learning that the short\-range "signal booster" is an actual Reaper. Shepard disembarks from the vehicle and sends the rest away to safety, with Legion wishing Shepard\-Commander good luck. Using the targeting laser, Normandy's targeting systems and the might of the Migrant Fleet, Shepard manages to destroy the Destroyer.

evidence.text: - Chris L'Etoile was the main writer for Legion in the second game, except for the confrontation with Tali. - Legion's design, notably the "N7 arm" and the hole in the torso, took inspiration from a concept art by Matt Rhodes depicting a cyborg Commander Shepard, an early idea for the resurrection plot of Mass Effect 2\. - Legion's name is a Biblical reference. In Mark chapter 5 Jesus spoke to a demon possessed man. 'Then Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”' \- Mark 5:9\. Legion explicitly refers to this in the dialog where Shepard asks it what its name is. - Shepard's N7 armor was originally added to the design concept just for fun, but has now become an integral part of Legion's appearance and back story. - The number of linked geth that make up Legion could possibly be a reference to the film THX 1138, the first film of Star Wars creator George Lucas. - Legion possesses a single antenna\-like attachment on its left shoulder, a trait shared with large bipedal geth units, such as the Juggernaut, who have two (one on each shoulder), but which is absent in man\-sized ones, such as the Shock Trooper. Although its exact function has yet to be revealed, it likely exists to emphasise the uniqueness of its mobile platform. - From time to time, Legion will do the Robot as one of its idle animations.\[1] This can happen in both the AI Core and on missions where Legion is in the Commander's squad. Legion will also beatbox during these animations. - It is possible to see Legion before its first appearance. After the two husks are killed by an unknown sniper on the derelict Reaper, if you look around in the back of the room the shots came from, Legion can be seen standing on the ledge at the back. It will walk away slowly once you enter the room. - Legion claims that Shepard encountered Sovereign on Ilos during the first game, even though this encounter actually happened on Virmire. It's uncertain whether this is a writing error, or if Legion simply has wrong information about the occurrence. - Legion is referred to by name in the subtitles when it first speaks on the derelict Reaper, but is otherwise listed as "Geth" until the name is suggested onboard the Normandy. - Legion's platform designation is 2A93, which is the hexadecimal equivalent of 10,899\. - As a sapient machine, Legion has been the subject of pronoun confusion both in\- and out\- of universe. - Curiously, at several points in conversations and during missions, Legion refers to itself as "I" rather than "we". The Geth VI was a network of geth virtual intelligences created by the "true" geth to study the Reapers. It appeared in Mass Effect 3 in place of Legion if Legion had been sold to Cerberus or never activated in Mass Effect 2, or if Legion joined Shepard's team but did not survive the Collector Base suicide mission. During the final operation on Rannoch a peaceful outcome was impossible when the Geth VI was present. evidence.text: Although its orange sun is only about 90% the mass of Sol and half as luminous, **Rannoch** is arid by Earth standards because it formed closer to its star and has slightly less ocean coverage. Photosynthetic life is concentrated around rivers and oceans, with large expanses of desert in between. The importance of plant life and shade in ancient quarian culture is evident in the translation of Rannoch's name\-\-"walled garden." To a starship's sensors, the most obvious feature of the quarian homeworld is the numerous heat sources in orbit. Thousands of geth space stations watch over the planet. Somewhere in this artificial swarm of constructions lurks the geth armada, waiting for its moment to counterattack.

Rannoch was the former quarian homeworld, the first planet of the Tikkun system in the Perseus Veil. It orbited an older orange star about 90% the mass of Sol and half as luminous, but because it formed closer to its star and had slightly less ocean coverage it was arid by Earth standards, with photosynthetic life concentrated around rivers and oceans and large deserts between. The importance of plant life and shade in ancient quarian culture is reflected in the planet's name, which translates as "walled garden." Reaching Rannoch in Mass Effect 3 required the mission Priority: Perseus Veil.

Almost three hundred years before the games, the quarians were driven from Rannoch by the geth, synthetic servants who gained sapience and rebelled against their creators. Rannoch became largely uninhabited, though the geth acted as caretakers, repairing the planet's ecology, restoring ancient structures, and cultivating farmland. Thousands of geth space stations watched over the planet, and the geth armada lurked among them awaiting a chance to counterattack. Rannoch had no insect life, so its pollinating plants evolved to rely on animals for propagation; this flora-fauna symbiosis is blamed for the quarians' weakened immune systems, which made colonizing other worlds extremely difficult after their exile, making reclamation of Rannoch a cultural and physiological necessity.

Native lifeforms included the qorach, a carnivorous bighorn-sheep analogue whose belly was always coated in blue-green fern pollen and seed casings, whose blind newborn was called a ke'sed; the lemek worm, a planarian analogue covered in metallic rose-colored scales that could regrow from pieces; and the fa'yin, an edible nut dating to the era of the first proto-quarian beasts. Rannoch was the setting for the missions Priority: Rannoch, Rannoch: Admiral Koris, and Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons.

Now that the quarians are reduced to a small, insular population, they have one common language known as Khelish. Words from the language listed below are taken from intra\-quarian conversation. - *bosh'tet* — curse/insult, likely being relative to "son\-of\-a\-bitch" or "bastard". - *esu se'lai* — likely a form of "goodbye" - *geth* — "Servant of the People" - *Mered'vai Rannoch* — "Forget Rannoch" - *nar* \[ship\-name] — child of - *nedas* — nowhere - *keelah* — "By the homeworld" - *keelah se'lai* — "By the homeworld I hope to see one day." - *keelah si'yah* — "By the homeworld I hope to find one day." - *ke'sed* (or *kes'ed*) — offspring of the qorach animal, figuratively means "naive" when used on people - *Pallu'Kaziel* — "Nevertheless, Justice Comes" - *Rannoch* — "walled garden" - *tasi* — no\-one - *tiral azhana* — "handful of water" - *vas* \[ship\-name] — crew of - *von* — "one who has a weak bladder" Quarian names are composed of four parts—the quarian's given name and clan name separated by an apostrophe, the title ("nar" means "child of", referring to their birth ship, while "vas", adopted after the quarian has completed their Pilgrimage and joined a ship, means "crew of") and the name of their vessel. When Tali first met Shepard, for instance, she was going by the name of her birth ship (the Rayya) because at that point she had not yet completed her Pilgrimage and was thus not yet able to join a quarian crew. Later, though, she became known as "Tali'Zorah vas Neema", indicating that she had completed her Pilgrimage and was welcome to join the Neema. On occasion quarians may impose their naming conventions on other races. Commander Shepard, for example, may be referred to as "Shepard vas Normandy" if the Commander chooses to interact with the quarians on their home territory. In certain formal situations, quarians appear to use both their adult ship and childhood ship. Tali'Zorah identifies herself as "Tali'Zorah vas Neema nar Rayya" during docking procedures following summons to the Migrant Fleet regarding accusations of treason.

Delivering it to the C-Sec officer gave 5 Reputation, 30 experience, and 1,000 credits, and updated the Citadel Defense Force War Asset.

The Citadel Tower stood at the centre of the Citadel, rising parallel to the Wards, and was the station's most distinctive monument and the seat of the Citadel Council, from which all Council decisions were made. It was reached by an elevator on the Presidium near the Relay Monument or from any Citadel Rapid Transit point. The Tower housed the Council Chambers, filled with trees and fountains, with anteroom staircases leading up to the Council's audience chamber; in Mass Effect: Revelation this area was called the Petitioner's Stage, beneath which lay a garden protected by glass. Politicians and petitioners such as Rear Admiral Kahoku gathered there, and Commander Shepard could overhear a salarian and a turian discussing rumours of Saren Arterius' involvement in Eden Prime and the volus bid for a Council seat, which the salarian rated as next to none. According to the VI Avina, the keepers frequently passed through the Tower and Council Chambers on their way elsewhere. The Tower was also used to manually open the Citadel's relay leading to dark space; when Sovereign attacked the station, it settled on the Tower and extruded cables into it. The Council Chambers were the site of the final confrontation between Shepard and Saren: pursuing him to the station's master control unit in the audience chamber, Shepard saw Saren die and fall through the glass into the garden below, after which his transformation into Sovereign's avatar collapsed the stage and the squad destroyed the creature in the garden. When Sovereign was destroyed by the Alliance and the remaining Citadel Fleet, a large piece of debris crashed into the Tower, nearly burying and crushing Shepard's team before a rescue party led by Captain Anderson found them.

Bonuses and penalties to Quarian war assets are exactly the same, just in the opposite direction (3 x \+50 if destroyed or 3 x \-50 if rewritten). This means, if you choose to make peace and acquire both geth and quarian help, your maximum War Asset value will be the same any way you decide here. After Priority: Geth Dreadnought, Shepard can inquire to Legion about the heretics. Legion will inform Shepard about the consequence of their actions. However, if Legion had died in the suicide mission, the Geth VI will respond in confusion as to why Legion deferred the choice of the heretics' fate to an organic. During Priority: Rannoch, when the time comes to choose between siding with the geth or quarians or resolving the conflict peacefully, the fate of the heretics is one of the numerous factors in whether peace will be a possibility or not. Destroying the heretics works in favour of peace, but isn't required. Admiral Zaal'Koris vas Qwib-Qwib was a member of the quarian Admiralty Board, outspoken in his sympathy for the geth. He firmly opposed reclaiming the quarian homeworld, arguing that the sentient geth had as much right to live as the quarians and that the Migrant Fleet should colonize a new world instead. This earned him the label of geth apologist; Han'Gerrel vas Neema called him a "whining suit-wetter" and Daro'Xen vas Moreh considered him a coward. He was initially distrustful of Rael'Zorah and his daughter Tali, though he later admitted he never hated Tali and only opposed her father's aim of war against the geth. His home vessel, the Qwib-Qwib, was a formerly owned ship whose embarrassing registry name he refused to change over "petty insults."

During Tali'Zorah's treason hearing in Mass Effect 2, Koris objected to Commander Shepard defending her, saying a human had no business in sensitive quarian military matters; Shala'Raan overruled him because Tali had been declared crew of the Normandy SR-2. If Shepard brought Legion, Koris instead demanded the geth be removed from the courtroom and accused Tali of intimidation, but withdrew when reminded the Rayya's captain had permitted Legion aboard. Koris was quick to conclude Shepard and Tali had died retaking the Alarei and moved to have Tali posthumously exiled, prompting objections from Raan and Gerrel before the pair returned alive.

In Mass Effect 3, the other admirals attacked the geth over Koris's objections, driving the geth to the Reapers; Koris feared this had doomed the quarian race and took command of the Civilian Fleet. His ship was shot down while destroying a geth planetary cannon; he survived the crash but was cut off from his crew. Shepard could obey his plea to save his crew instead of him, or convince him to return. If rescued, Koris talked panicking captains into staying, contributed to the war effort, and backed Shepard in brokering quarian-geth peace, lending his authority when Shepard ordered all quarian ships to cease fire. If left, he died charging a Geth Prime with a primed grenade, and some Civilian Fleet captains fled and were cut down, reducing quarian combat effectiveness.

Rannoch: Admiral Koris was a Mass Effect 3 mission available after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and only before Priority: Rannoch. During the dreadnought debrief, Admiral Shala'Raan reported that Zaal'Koris had sacrificed his ship to destroy a geth planetary defense cannon, crash-landing on Rannoch and leaving the quarian Civilian Fleet without a leader; many Civilian Fleet captains planned to break formation and make a run for the mass relay past the geth guns. Shepard offered to land and rescue him.

En route, Admiral Daro'Xen reported the Civilian Fleet had taken losses and that Koris's escape pod had crashed within range of a jamming tower before communications cut. Steve Cortez's shuttle was driven off by anti-aircraft guns, so Shepard's squad disabled the AA guns on foot so Cortez could destroy the jamming tower. The mission was an incursion into geth territory with heavy shielded synthetics, armored support, Geth Primes, cloaked Geth Hunters, and numerous Geth Trip Mines. Along the way the squad found a Javelin and other salvage and encountered Dorn'Hazt, a mortally wounded quarian from Koris's ship, who explained that the Civilian Fleet had not wanted war with the geth and might flee without Koris's leadership before directing Shepard to Koris's position. Data retrieved along the route unlocked the Target Jamming Technology objective.

Contacted by shuttle, Koris refused rescue and demanded Shepard save his crew instead; with sufficient Reputation he could be persuaded to be picked up. Letting Koris die cost his leadership and, if the quarians survived, caused the Civilian Fleet to panic; it could also make quarian-geth peace impossible depending on other choices. Whatever the choice, Shepard manned a shuttle turret and shot down Geth Rocket Troopers and their missiles, which were actually aimed at the shuttle, until the rescued party was aboard. If Koris died, the Quarian Civilian Fleet war asset lost 75 Military Strength; if he survived he was added as a war asset worth 25. If Javik was present he was found in the AI Core arguing with EDI. After the first of the two Rannoch missions, Raan argued with Han'Gerrel; after the second, Xen argued with Tali, with Shepard's support affecting the Quarian Heavy Fleet, Advanced AI Relays, and Paragon rewards. Completing the mission with Koris alive produced a thank-you email from Captain Nav'Teel vas Ghrigult, Dorn'Hazt's cousin. The mission was written by Sylvia Feketekuty.

Many dropships are seen defending the Geth Dreadnought and participating in attacks on quarian vessels during the quarian campaign to retake Rannoch from the geth. Geth Dropships form part of the mobilized geth armada and are used against the synthetics' enemies.

- If Admiral Koris dies, the Quarian Civilian Fleet War Asset will be reduced by 75 Military Strength. Also, depending on your other choices, it may not be possible to make peace between the quarians and geth at the end of Priority: Rannoch. - If Admiral Koris survives, he is added as a War Asset worth 25 Military Strength. - If Javik is present, he will be found in the AI Core arguing with EDI. Shepard can choose to "support" one or the other. - Regardless of which mission you do first (Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons or **Rannoch: Admiral Koris**), the two arguments below will occur in this order: - After the first completed mission, Admiral Raan starts arguing with Admiral Gerrel. Shepard can choose to "support" one or the other. Supporting Admiral Raan **reduces** the value of the Quarian Heavy Fleet war asset by 10\. Supporting Admiral Gerrel **increases** the value of the same by 25\. - After the second completed mission, Admiral Xen starts arguing with Tali. Shepard can choose to "support" one or the other. Supporting Admiral Xen gives you the Advanced AI Relays war asset worth 45 war assets, meanwhile supporting Tali will provide 2 Paragon points.

codex.text: - Rannoch's name translates to "walled garden," reflecting the significance of plant life and shade in ancient quarian cultural values. (source: Rannoch)

- Rannoch is the quarian homeworld, overrun by the geth in the Morning War and left behind the Perseus Veil for three centuries while the geth tended its abandoned buildings like a cemetery. At the 2186 Battle of Rannoch, Shepard and the Normandy cracked open the Reaper base transmitting upgrades to the geth and Shepard alone held its Destroyer off until the quarian fleet's finishing volley; the outcome then hinged on whether the rescued geth unit was allowed to upload the Reaper code, deciding between quarian near-annihilation, geth destruction, or a fragile peace (see `scenes/rannoch-the-choice-above-the-fleet.yaml`). (source: Geth War; Codex/The Reaper War)

- Rannoch was the former quarian homeworld, first planet of the Tikkun system in the Perseus Veil; its name translates as "walled garden," reflecting the cultural importance of plant life and shade. (source: Rannoch)

- Admiral Zaal'Koris crashed his personal flagship into a Rannoch antiship cannon that was devastating the Migrant Fleet and survived pinned down on the surface; read `scenes/rannoch-admiral-koris.yaml` rather than a bullet for the rescue mission, since whether he lives or dies fighting there swings Civilian Fleet strength and possibly quarian-geth peace. (source: Migrant Fleet)

- In Mass Effect 3 the quarians destroyed the geth megastructure at Rannoch, and the weakened geth accepted Reaper control code to survive; for the three endings — Legion's death, the quarian fleet burning, or peace bought by Legion's self-sacrifice — read `scenes/rannoch-the-choice-above-the-fleet.yaml` rather than a bullet: the causality does not survive compression. (source: Geth)

- Priority: Rannoch: Shepard used a prototype targeting laser to guide Normandy and quarian fleet fire that destroyed a Reaper base controlling the geth and killed a Reaper Destroyer on the ground, then mediated the final quarian-geth confrontation, which could end in the extinction of either race or, with sufficient reputation and trust, a lasting peace with both fleets joining the war (source: Priority: Rannoch).
